items.q: How much does it cost to paint a house in Bellevue?

a.text: Bellevue exteriors typically run $5,000 to $12,000 and interiors $3,500 to $25,000. Bellevue spans an unusually wide range of housing — a Crossroads rambler and a Somerset or Bridle Trails custom home are not the same project, and an honest estimate reflects that rather than applying a flat per-square-foot rate.
a.html: Bellevue exteriors typically run $5,000 to $12,000 and interiors $3,500 to $25,000. a.text: What actually drives the number: the condition of the existing coating, the siding material, the number of stories, the amount of trim and detail work, and how much carpentry repair surfaces once we start washing. items.q: Can I see paint colors in person before I commit?

a.text: Yes — and this is genuinely unusual for a painting contractor. Our Bellevue location at 3700 Factoria Blvd SE is next door to Sherwin-Williams. You can sit down with us, talk through the project, then walk next door and look at real samples under real light.
a.html: Yes — and this is genuinely unusual for a painting contractor. Our Bellevue location at 3700 Factoria Blvd SE is next door to Sherwin-Williams. You can sit down with us, talk through the project, then walk next door and look at real samples under real light.

a.text: Colors that look right on a phone screen frequently look wrong on a wall. North-facing Pacific Northwest rooms pull cool and grey in ways that surprise people, and an exterior color chosen indoors often reads two shades darker outside under overcast sky. Seeing large samples in person, and living with them on the actual wall for a couple of days, prevents the most expensive mistake in painting: repainting.

a.text: Many do. Somerset, Newport Hills, Lakemont, and a number of the Bridle Trails and Woodridge communities maintain approved palettes and require architectural review before exterior work begins.

items.q: How often should a Bellevue home be repainted?

a.text: Exteriors generally need attention every 7 to 12 years here, though south and west elevations often need it sooner than the rest of the house. Interiors depend entirely on use — high-traffic areas every 3 to 5 years, low-traffic rooms considerably longer.
a.html: Exteriors generally need attention every 7 to 12 years here, though south and west elevations often need it sooner than the rest of the house. Interiors depend entirely on use — high-traffic areas every 3 to 5 years, low-traffic rooms considerably longer.

a.text: Do not wait for a calendar date. Chalking that comes off on your hand, hairline cracking, caulk pulling away from trim joints, or any bare wood showing means the coating has stopped protecting the substrate. Repainting at that point is maintenance. Waiting past it turns it into carpentry, which costs several times more.

nodes.text: A Little Bit About Bellevue
Bellevue: Where Urban Energy Meets Natural Beauty

Situated on the eastern shores of Lake Washington, directly across from Seattle, Bellevue, Washington, is a thriving city that seamlessly blends urban vibrancy with natural beauty. Nicknamed "The City of Lights," Bellevue boasts a population of over 152,000 residents and is the fifth-largest city in Washington State.

nodes.text: A Rich History and Modern Flourishing

Bellevue's history can be traced back to the mid-1800s, when it was primarily a center for logging and coal mining. In the latter half of the 20th century, the city experienced significant growth, transforming into a major hub for technology and commerce. Today, Bellevue is a dynamic city brimming with Fortune 500 companies, thriving businesses, and a diverse population.
